contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Goal denied at 0-0 in a 1-0 game, but the decision went against Real Madrid, who won anyway; it cannot have changed the winner.

contested_decisions.description: Havertz's opening goal: in the build-up the ball (struck by Marquinhos) hit Leandro Trossard's arm before reaching Havertz; goal stood, VAR did not intervene.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: beIN Sports match report (noted the arm contact, no verdict); Archivo VAR (Spanish refereeing analysts) quoted by dailysports.net said it should have been disallowed; no UEFA statement found
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Goal counted in a match drawn 1-1 and decided on penalties. However the decision favoured Arsenal and PSG won anyway, so it cannot have cost PSG the trophy.

contested_decisions.description: From a PSG corner the ball struck Bukayo Saka's chest then arm in the Arsenal box; no penalty given.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: no expert assessment found; journalist comments only (beIN described it as accidental)
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: Would have been a penalty chance at 0-1 in a one-goal game. However the decision favoured Arsenal and PSG won anyway, so it cannot have cost PSG the trophy.

contested_decisions.description: Cristhian Mosquera, already booked (47'), tripped Kvaratskhelia for the PSG penalty; no second yellow card shown. Penalty itself widely viewed as correct. Mosquera was substituted at 66'.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: Graham Scott (ex-Premier League referee, for The Athletic) said PSG had 'a strong case for a second yellow card'; ESPN VAR review called the penalty award correct
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: A second yellow would have left Arsenal with ten men for about 55 minutes plus extra time in a match drawn 1-1 and lost on penalties. However the decision favoured Arsenal and PSG won anyway, so it cannot have cost PSG the trophy.

contested_decisions.description: Noni Madueke went down under a challenge from behind by Nuno Mendes in the PSG box; Siebert waved play on and VAR did not intervene. Arteta and Rice booked for protesting. Arteta said it 'easily can be a penalty'.
contested_decisions.assessed_by: ESPN VAR review: 'got the call right, but it was close'; Graham Scott (The Athletic): some angles suggest an offence, others don't, VAR would not have overturned either way
contested_decisions.impact_reasoning: A penalty at 1-1 late in extra time could directly have decided a match settled by a shootout.
